subject: OptiMed capacity top-up and co-term pricing request
messages:
From: Seth Miller <seth@optimed.com>

Cc: procurement@optimed.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity increase mid-quarter — pricing & co-term?

Marcus —

Quick one: we had a product sprint and need to increase our token capacity ~2.5x for the next 3 months starting July 1. We're currently mid-year and would prefer to co-term with our existing annual contract rather than create a separate short-term seat. Can you share: 1) pro-rated pricing for the partial quarter top-up, 2) any volume discount you can apply for this temporary uplift, and 3) whether you can split the invoice (one for the uplift, one for regular monthly commit)?

We're also open to an upfront coupon/credit model if that helps avoid double invoicing for our finance team — we'd need a clear invoice path for our AP.

If possible, can you send a sketch by end of day Monday? Procurement is cc'd.

Thanks,
Seth Miller
Head of Platform
OptiMed Solutions

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Seth Miller <seth@optimed.com>
Cc: procurement@optimed.com, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity increase mid-quarter — pricing & co-term?

Seth — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the sprint. Short summary of practical options below; attaching a simple amendment sketch for your legal/procurement team to review.

Option A — Pro-rated top-up (fastest)
- Temporary top-up billed pro-rata for the remainder of your billing month.
- Unit price: standard usage rate with a 10% uplift discount on the incremental token units for the 3-month window.
- Invoice: single invoice with line items separated (base commit + pro-rated top-up).

Option B — Voucher/credit (single invoice)
- Redwood issues a prepaid top-up voucher (credit) for the uplift amount; voucher is applied to usage and shows as credit on your monthly invoice.
- Financial benefit: avoids needing a separate PO for a short-term invoice; can be amortized in your accounting.
- Suggested credit sizing: purchase a 3-month forecast at a 15% effective discount versus pay-as-you-go.

Option C — Temporary committed uplift + co-term
- Increase committed capacity now and co-term to align with your annual renewal; we can offer a 20% uplift discount on the newly committed portion if you convert the uplift into a 12-month committed add-on (effective if you agree before June 25).
- Requires an amendment; I attached a draft (amendment_proposal_v1.pdf).

Operational notes:
- We can split invoices as you requested; finance can receive a 'one-time top-up' invoice plus the regular monthly commit invoice.
- If procurement prefers a single bill, Option B (voucher) is easiest.

I've looped in Lauren (revops) for billing/credit approval. Ben (CS lead) can help scope the KV/cache settings to reduce cost while you spike usage. If you want, we can lock the offer above for 72 hours while legal reviews.

Attachments: amendment_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal), optimed_usage_q2.csv (your file)

Best,
Marcus Lin

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 18:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: OptiMed capacity increase — quick pricing approval request

FYI forwarding Seth's ask — OptiMed wants a 2.5x temporary top-up for 3 months starting 7/1. They prefer co-term but will accept voucher/credit. My ask: can we approve Option C at a 20% uplift discount (on the new committed portion) if they convert to a 12mo add-on? If not, would a 15% prepaid voucher (Option B) be acceptable as a fallback?

Rationale: customer is strategic (medical SaaS), strong usage signals, likely to expand beyond this spike. Approving 20% on a committed conversion protects unit economics long-term versus short-lived usage discounts. We'll also include one month of premium onboarding support for free to help them migrate KV cache and batching.

Costs/impact: estimated incremental ARR if converted = $120k/year. If they go voucher-only with 15% discount, revenue recognition is earlier but lower ARR.

Can you confirm by EOD so I can lock pricing for 72 hours and get a countersign path to procurement?

— Marcus

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 19:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: OptiMed capacity increase — quick pricing approval request

Marcus — approved with conditions.
1) 20% on the committed conversion (Option C) is acceptable, but only if legal can sign the simple amendment we attached (amendment_proposal_v1.pdf) with a 12-month minimum on the uplift. No retro discounts.
2) Include the one month premium onboarding credit but cap any further support credits — we want to avoid normalizing credits as discounts.
3) If OptiMed insists on voucher-only (Option B), maximum discount is 15% and finance must confirm the invoice/credit treatment (we need a PO + payment terms up front).

Ben — help Marcus scope the onboarding deliverable and provide an estimated time commitment. Marcus — once you have procurement's preference, I'll route to Legal for a quick review and Ops for billing pathing.

— Lauren

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Final offer: OptiMed mid-cycle uplift (co-term path)

Seth / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per our options and internal approvals, here's the firm offer:

1) Co-term committed conversion (recommended) — Option C
- Increase committed capacity now to cover the 2.5x uplift.
- Discount on new committed add-on: 20% (applies only to the newly committed capacity).
- Term: 12 months minimum from amendment execution.
- Billing: added as an amendment (one combined invoice monthly that shows base commit + committed add-on).
- Next steps: I have attached amendment_proposal_v1.pdf — if you confirm acceptance, I'll route this to Legal and DocuSign. We can hold this pricing for 72 hours.

2) Voucher/credit (alternate) — Option B
- Prepaid credit for estimated 3-month uplift; discount 15% if purchased upfront.
- Billing: single invoice for credit purchase; credit applied monthly to usage.

3) Pro-rated top-up (fallback) — Option A
- Billed pro-rata for remaining days; incremental volume priced at standard with 10% uplift discount.

Attachments: amendment_proposal_v1.pdf, OptiMed_SOW_v2.pdf (for reference)

Please let me know which option procurement prefers and I will send the appropriate PO/invoice template and DocuSign link. If you go with Option C we need a signed amendment by June 25 to secure the 20% rate.

Regards,
